Well, send our engineer up there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если что-то не так, персонал штрафуют.
examples.trans: If something goes wrong, they fine the staff.

examples.text: Даже если простишь, то никогда не забудешь.
examples.trans: Even if you forgive, you will never forget it.

examples.text: А если вдруг объявится настоящий тайный гость?
examples.trans: What if the real secret guest suddenly shows up?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если что-то не так, персонал штрафуют.
examples.trans: If something goes wrong, they fine the staff.
Has something happened?
Somehow I'm tired.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Гости ресторана — это не только посетители.
examples.trans: Restaurant guests are not just casual visitors.

examples.text: Кто-то не хочет вставать с кровати.
examples.trans: Someone does not want to get out of bed.

examples.text: Утренняя смена на кухне уже началась!
examples.trans: The morning shift in the kitchen has already started!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Who is this secret guest?

examples.text: Если что-то не так, персонал штрафуют.
examples.trans: If something goes wrong, they fine the staff.
I hope we will avoid such conversations.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'staff' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Если что-то не так, персонал штрафуют.
examples.trans: If something goes wrong, they fine the staff.
This is a delicious lunch for the staff.

examples.text: Сегодня обед для персонала готовит наш огузок.
examples.trans: Today our runt is cooking lunch for the staff.

meanings.en: to fine, penalize, impose a fine on
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'they fine', paired with 'оштрафовать'.

examples.trans: The director fines the dishonest cook.

examples.text: Я штрафую тебя на двести тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: I am fining you two hundred thousand rubles.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: In a hotel there are always breakfasts.

examples.text: Что ты забыл на моей кухне?
examples.trans: What did you lose in my kitchen?

examples.text: Я делаю за тебя твою работу.
examples.trans: I am doing your job for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'one's own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: За своих подчинённых я не волнуюсь.
examples.trans: I do not worry about my subordinates.

examples.text: Миша, иди ты в свой кабинет.
examples.trans: Misha, go to your own office.
Drink up your delicious coffee!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'чинённый'). Common masculine noun meaning 'subordinates' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: За своих подчинённых я не волнуюсь.
examples.trans: I do not worry about my subordinates.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть подчинённый.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always subordinates.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is located right here.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?
The cooks have to get up early.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'I worry'.

examples.trans: Don't worry.
I'm nervous.
Don't worry, I won't.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: I'm going home.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что ты забыл на моей кухне?
examples.trans: What did you lose in my kitchen?

examples.text: Миша, иди ты в свой кабинет.
examples.trans: Misha, go to your own office.
You were upset because of yesterday.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Before you is our new hotel.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.
In a hotel there are always breakfasts.

meanings.note: From French 'cabinet' (private study or office).

examples.text: Миша, иди ты в свой кабинет.
examples.trans: Misha, go to your own office.
I'm in the office.
This is the mayor's office.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Через десять минут у нас собрание.
examples.trans: In ten minutes we have a meeting.
You were upset because of yesterday.
Yesterday's grand opening was a total failure.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'ten', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Через десять минут у нас собрание.
examples.trans: In ten minutes we have a meeting.
In ten minutes.
Ten roubles.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minutes' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Через десять минут у нас собрание.
examples.trans: In ten minutes we have a meeting.

examples.text: Спасибо, я верну телефон через минуту!
examples.trans: Thanks, I will return the phone in a minute!
Mom, wait one minute.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We get up early every morning.
They are too lazy to come down to the restaurant!

examples.text: Утренняя смена на кухне уже началась!
examples.trans: The morning shift in the kitchen has already started!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.
We get up early every morning.
We must feed all the guests.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обрание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Через десять минут у нас собрание.
examples.trans: In ten minutes we have a meeting.
In the morning there is a meeting in the kitchen.
Attention, cooks! Let us begin our meeting.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All our management will be there.
Mikhail, there is a small problem there.
What is happening over there right now?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.text: В моём отеле должен быть идеальный порядок!
examples.trans: There must be ideal order in my hotel!
I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All our management will be there.
No, everything is fine.
Calm down, everything is fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Before you is our new hotel.
Our restaurant is located right here.
A bit faster, well, where is our bacon?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'management' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: All our management will be there.
The leadership made a new decision.

examples.text: Но почему руководство нас совсем не ценит?
examples.trans: But why does leadership not value us at all?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ообщить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'they informed'.

examples.trans: They informed me of important news.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и сообщить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and they informed on time.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.trans: They informed me of important news.

examples.text: Для важного гостя нам ничего не жалко!
examples.trans: Nothing is too good for an important guest!
It's an important question.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'news' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They informed me of important news.
Good news!
Watch the news.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('secret, undercover').

examples.trans: Who is this secret guest?

examples.text: Тайный гость будет сегодня или завтра.
examples.trans: The secret guest will be here today or tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы должны встретить тайного гостя достойно.
examples.trans: We must welcome the secret guest properly.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Гости ресторана — это не только посетители.
examples.trans: Restaurant guests are not just casual visitors.
We must feed all the guests.
Who is this secret guest?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: I will eat at work today.

examples.text: Тайный гость будет сегодня или завтра.
examples.trans: The secret guest will be here today or tomorrow.
Be on alert today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'or', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They informed me of important news.

examples.text: Тайный гость будет сегодня или завтра.
examples.trans: The secret guest will be here today or tomorrow.

examples.text: Я должен рассказать Кате или нет?
examples.trans: Should I tell Katya or not?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.trans: In a hotel there are always breakfasts.

examples.text: Тайный гость будет сегодня или завтра.
examples.trans: The secret guest will be here today or tomorrow.
We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чеку').

examples.trans: Be on alert today.

examples.text: Иначе этих двоих было не примирить.
examples.trans: Otherwise there was no way to reconcile those two.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'большой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small').

examples.trans: Mikhail, there is a small problem there.

examples.text: В номере у нас небольшая проблемка.
examples.trans: We have a small problem in the room.

examples.text: Это небольшой комплимент от нашего заведения.
examples.trans: This is a small gift from our establishment.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'блемка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'little problem' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Mikhail, there is a small problem there.

examples.text: О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
examples.trans: Report any problems to me immediately.
He is solving problems with suppliers.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'complain'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и жаловаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and complain on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют жаловаться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to complain.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Before you is our new hotel.
Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Гости ресторана — это не только посетители.
examples.trans: Restaurant guests are not just casual visitors.

meanings.en: strong, powerful (also used as a noun: the strong)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strong, severe').

examples.trans: The guests are complaining about the bitter cold.

examples.text: Сильный ищет способ, а слабый ищет причину.
examples.trans: The strong man looks for a way, and the weak man looks for an excuse.
A strong wind was blowing outside.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cold' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The guests are complaining about the bitter cold.
It is very cold here in the room.
Stop chatting nonsense in the cold!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A bit faster, well, where is our bacon?
Wake up everyone, morning has already arrived.

examples.text: За своих подчинённых я не волнуюсь.
examples.trans: I do not worry about my subordinates.

meanings.en: to send (a person, a letter, a message)
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'править'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'send', paired with 'отправлять'.

examples.trans: I sent the letter.
Send me a message.

examples.text: И бабушку на лечение в Израиль отправил.
examples.trans: And he sent our grandmother to Israel for treatment.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, send our engineer up there.
Our head chef went in there.
Better let Lyova go up there.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'engineer' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Well, send our engineer up there.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть инженер.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always engineer.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A bit faster, well, where is our bacon?
We are frying, frying our bacon.

examples.text: Он проверяет работу всех служб отеля.
examples.trans: He inspects the work of all hotel departments.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'yourself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Could he not think of that himself?
This happened in front of the prefect himself.

examples.text: Это и есть тот самый тайный гость?
examples.trans: Is that really the secret guest?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Меня зовут Михаил. Чем я могу вам помочь?
examples.trans: My name is Mikhail. How can I help you?
I can't today.
That can't be.

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (it over)', paired with 'думать'.

examples.trans: Could he not think of that himself?
Here is what I thought last night.

examples.text: Виктория Сергеевна, я тут вот что подумал.
examples.trans: Victoria Sergeevna, here is what I just thought.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

examples.trans: We must feed all the guests.

examples.text: Мы должны встретить тайного гостя достойно.
examples.trans: We must welcome the secret guest properly.

examples.text: В моём отеле должен быть идеальный порядок!
examples.trans: There must be ideal order in my hotel!

meanings.en: to meet, to pick up (at a station)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'третить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to meet', paired with 'встречать'.

examples.text: Мы должны встретить тайного гостя достойно.
examples.trans: We must welcome the secret guest properly.

examples.text: Меня никто не встретил на вокзале.
examples.trans: Nobody met me at the station.
I will meet you at the entrance.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы должны встретить тайного гостя достойно.
examples.trans: We must welcome the secret guest properly.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно достойно и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite worthily and calmly.
